title: CAT 49: Game Flow Dynamics & Game Script Detection
source: PLOS One 2025, YouTube (BBall Index, Cleaning the Glass)
summary: Track game flow phases (early, mid, late), halftime margin as predictor, and garbage time detection. Game flow affects pace, shot selection, and effort. 8 features: halftime margin, game phase momentum, lead trading frequency, garbage time flag.

title: CAT 53: Rest & Fatigue - Nonlinear Effects
summary: Add nonlinear rest transforms and exponential fatigue decay. Rest diminishing returns are real: rest^2 captures this. Cumulative fatigue using exponential decay over 7-14 days better than linear rolling averages.

title: CAT 61: Vegas Consensus & Market Line Efficiency
source: Sports AI 2026, Covers consensus, betting market theory
summary: Implied probability consensus across books, line movement magnitude, and sharp vs public divergence. Vegas lines incorporate 90% of info but market micro adds non-redundant signal. 6 features: consensus prob, movement, disagreement, steam signals.

title: CAT 47: Advanced Clutch Performance Metrics
summary: Clutch performance has measurable predictive power. Estimation of Clutch Competency (ECC) metric combines scoring, defense, ORB minus TOV. 3-point accuracy drops under pressure. Late-game free throw reliability and close-game win % are strong signals.
data_source: nba_api historical logs, box scores with timestamps

title: CAT 48: Referee Crew Bias & Foul Calling Patterns
source: Belasen et al. 2025, Sabag et al. 2026 (MIT Sloan), NBER
summary: Home favoritism in foul calling is persistent and measurable. Each ref crew has bias profile: home foul delta, FTA advantage, total fouls per game (tight vs loose), and home win %. Recent 2026 studies confirm this is real and exploitable.
data_source: NBA.com L2M reports (requires scraper), official ref crew assignments

title: CAT 50: Market Microstructure & Sharp Money Signals
source: Sports AI 2026, Polymarket API, SBR closing lines, Covers
summary: Sharp money detection via steam moves, reverse line movement, and public divergence. Polymarket prediction markets provide independent signal. Late-money direction and closing line consensus are non-redundant with model. 14 features tracking market microstructure.
data_source: BetMGM/DraftKings APIs, Polymarket API, SBR closing lines archive

title: CAT 54: Shot Quality & Shot Location Distribution Splits
summary: Shot location is strongly predictive. Montrucchio's SOTA model includes xEFG (expected field goal % by zone). Rim vs mid-range vs 3-point distribution + efficiency. Shot quality delta (actual vs expected eFG%) is non-obvious predictor.
data_source: pbpstats shot data (API), nba_api zone stats, play-by-play analysis

title: CAT 57: Player Health & Injury Impact (Position-Weighted)
source: FiveThirtyEight RAPTOR, Seth Partnow (The Athletic), NBA injury reports
summary: Injuries are massive signal. WAR lost weighted by position importance (PG > C > SF). Key player return includes rust factor (days since return). Bench depth strength predicts replacement quality. Preseason lineup availability % affects model confidence.
data_source: NBA.com injury report, ESPN injury tracker, basketball-reference, nba_api

title: CAT 51: Lineup Continuity & Rotation Depth Analysis
source: MIT Sloan Lineup Analysis, NBA.com lineups, Rotowire
summary: Lineup quality matters. Starting lineup continuity %, bench net rating, rotation size (# players 10+ min). Best-performing 5-man combo efficiency and closing unit reliability predict outcomes.
data_source: NBA.com lineups API, nba_api game logs, historical lineups

title: CAT 52: Player Tracking & Hustle Metrics
source: NBA.com Hustle Stats (official 2025), player tracking APIs
summary: Hustle stats (official from NBA): contested shots %, deflections per 100 poss, screen assists. These measure effort and intensity. Tracking data available from nba_api endpoints. Defensive commitment (charges, help frequency) predict outcomes.
data_source: nba_api hustle stats endpoint, player tracking data

title: CAT 55: Head-to-Head & Historical Matchup Dynamics
source: Thinking Basketball empirical work, Sloan papers, historical analysis
summary: H2H history has signal but can be noisy. Recent 5-game H2H win %, 3-year overall H2H record, style clash (ORtg vs DRtg gap), and home-court effect in matchup are non-obvious predictors. Exponential decay weights recent games more.

title: CAT 56: Season Phase & Playoff Implications Context
summary: Season phase matters: playoff hunt vs eliminated affects effort. Nonlinear phase (sqrt of games played) captures acceleration in playoff race importance. Revenge game flag, back from road trip, and playoff implications scoring track contextual motivation.

title: CAT 58: Tempo Adjustment & Pace Dynamics
source: PLOS One 2025 pace study, ESPN BPI
summary: Pace is second-order but important. Pace trend (accelerating vs decelerating), transition rate vs half-court, and defensive pace imposed (slowing D) are predictive. Possession length variance measures unpredictability.

title: CAT 59: Defensive Efficiency by Position & Situation
source: Cleaning the Glass (Ben Falk), defensive analytics
summary: Defense is harder to model but position-specific D is real: perimeter D (3pt% allowed), paint D (PPG allowed), transition D, and drive D. Bench defense rating and defensive consistency (stable vs variable) are signals.
data_source: nba_api, Cleaning the Glass API (if available)

title: CAT 60: Bench & Role Player Production
summary: Bench scoring, bench net rating, role player usage, and backup PG reliability predict reserve minutes and impact. Trash time minutes % affects stat inflation. Starter overlap vs bench indicates rest patterns.

title: CAT 62: Player Fatigue & Usage Overload
source: Player load management studies, workload tracking
summary: Usage creep matters: star usage combined, star minutes load, usage rate spike vs season avg. Carry load indicator (dominant player carrying) may predict efficiency drops. Playing time balance affects performance stability.

title: CAT 63: Game Importance & Situational Context
summary: Motivation matters but is subtle. Playoff implications score (WP swing), conference/division games, national TV flag, revenge factor, and composite motivation track context. Hard to model but non-zero effect.

title: CAT 64: Tempo-Adjusted Efficiency Metrics
source: Dean Oliver Four Factors, KenPom (college basketball)
summary: Pace-free analysis separates efficiency from pace. Tempo-free ORTG/DRTG, per-possession PPP, and pace-adjusted net rating may reduce multicollinearity. Relatively low expected gain but conceptually clean.
